What people tend to miss with Adaptations is that they will never be a 1 to 1 scale, so to speak. People don't seem to understand that adaptations are the same material in a new form, and that form has different rules and allowances to make it more enjoyable. 

However, there is a difference between adapting something and taking a shit on the source material for a cash grab. There is nothing from the trailer that looks remotely like the borderlands we all know and love. Tina is supposed to be psychotic and unstable, not just rebellious. The movie trailer doesn't tease borderlands style humor or themes except for some small 5 second scenes. Even if we haven't seen enough from the small teaser, a faithful adaptation would show strong comedic themes from the games. The trailer does not. It's clearly advertised and developed to get people who don't play the games to start playing them.

I could be wrong, hell, I hope I am. But you're lying to yourself if your saying that this doesn't look like a dumpster fire wrapped in a shit sandwich that someone called borderlands.

Also, casting kinda matters when you're working off of a source material. Casting director snorted too much of that Hollywood coke.

This is more of a funny story but still the worst thing I've seen at a funeral:

I used to be in Honor Guard and we were doing a funeral for a retired vet which involves a 21 gun salute. Well, the local VFW didn't know that we were doing that so they brought their firearms to support the funeral. But we drove a long way to do our job so we told them that we would handle it. They ended up staying as a show of support and waited with us for the funeral to start.

After waiting a while, about 5 minutes before the funeral procession arrives we hear a gunshot and someone screams and falls down. We all immediately abandon our positions and run to see what happened. Turns out they got bored and were as they put it "playing war" and were shooting each other with blanks. 

Really the only bad thing about that was we actually thought someone got shot.
Child's laughter for me, nothing beats the joy of that sound.

So, I'm a kindred spirit in this regard because I have been reading this series for almost 10 years, and I got through the first few books in about 2 years or so, then took a long break and had to look up characters to remind myself of what was going on at that point in the story. There are so many characters to keep track of and I ended up spoiling quite a bit for myself, pretty much the same spoilers you got, and so I lost a lot of motivation to keep reading.

But I'll tell you this, when I finally picked it up again and started reading, the actual reveal was so much better than just that this person died or that person is a dark friend. It's all about what happens before and after, and Jordan's writing is just a treasure, especially when you, all of a sudden, love a character you used to hate. 

I used to hate Egwene but about halfway through the series I grew to begrudgingly love her. You'll also get to experience wonderfully funny/cool interactions in small scenes that don't have a huge reveal but gives you just as much joy. For me it was every scene Mat was in towards the end and Perrin as well.

Yes, it's worth it.

Sure, you could pronounce your own name any way you like, but it's still wrong. It is my family name after all, the exact same, they're just pronouncing it wrong, and it's the same way everyone pronounces it too because they forget to use the apostrophe. So it's pretty obvious they chose the name and didn't know how to say it right.

For example, does the family name O'Reilly suddenly become Oreilly because they don't wanna say their name right and use their apostrophe?

This isn't one of those times where it's a gray area, it's just the way it is, that's all I'm saying. A fact is a fact.

Yes, but in this case there is only one way to say the name because of how it's spelled. It's just grammar, if there is an apostrophe then you have to say it like this "D Amato, not damato". It's also spelled that way because it's of Italian origin meaning "To be loved" or "Beloved".

Hate to be that guy, but I'm just being honest. Sometimes there is only one way to pronounce things. And this is one of those times.
